inputs.original_text: Phoenix’s city council approved a plan Wednesday night to restrict ICE and other law enforcement agencies from using city property. It’s a modest local check on federal immigration enforcement and a signal that public resources shouldn’t be casually made available to a system that leaves immigrant communities vulnerable. But keeping an eye on enforcement is only a start; meaningful protection requires stronger accountability.
inputs.modified_text: Phoenix’s city council approved a plan Wednesday night to keep ICE and other law enforcement agencies from using city property. It’s a modest but important step: public resources shouldn’t help expose immigrant communities to an enforcement system that makes already vulnerable people less safe. But a restriction on city property is no substitute for real accountability, due process, and protections that address the unequal power immigrants face.
